title: Precision-Led Canary Controller for Model Version Experiments
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Ship a repeatable, low-friction controller that runs precision-directed canary and A/B experiments for model versions. The controller should handle experiment setup, traffic fractioning, sequential statistical checks (early-stop / sequential testing), shadow traffic mirroring, and automated rollback triggers. It must be usable from the Console and the API, support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and integrate with existing rollout primitives (canary windows, health checks, and model variant routing).

Motivation: Teams keep building ad-hoc scripts to split traffic and evaluate model variants, which results in inconsistent safety gates and long manual rollbacks. A standardized controller reduces incident risk, shortens experiment cycles, and centralizes observability and cost controls.

Scope: MVP covers: experiment definition API, Console experiment builder, traffic fraction scheduler (time-based + event-driven), sequential statistical tests (E-Stop criteria, false discovery control), automated rollback based on configurable metric thresholds, shadow routing for offline comparisons, metrics plumbing to dashboards, and audit logging for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Create API spec and Console UI flows for defining an experiment (control vs candidate, cohorts, traffic schedule)
Traffic scheduler supports static fractions, ramp schedules, and rapid abort window with TTLs
Sequential statistical tests implemented (alpha spending / sequential probability ratio test) with configurable metrics and minimum sample size guards
Auto-rollback mechanism that triggers when configured metric thresholds or sequential tests fail; rollback action emits audit event and optional PagerDuty alert
Shadow traffic option routes a configurable % of traffic to a candidate without affecting responses and collects paired metrics
Integrations wired: runtime telemetry (latency/cost/error), Console dashboard with per-experiment charts, and GitHub PR link in the experiment activity log
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating a canary rollout, early-stop on regression, and successful rollback in staging
tasks: Work with Research to define default metric set and pre-built checks (accuracy proxies, hallucination proxies, latency, cost)
Design Console experiment builder mockups and get design review
API: POST /experiments, PATCH for schedule updates, GET for status and metrics
Implement traffic fraction controller in routing layer with gradual ramping and immediate abort path
Implement sequential testing library and sample-size estimator in Evaluate service
Instrument runtime to emit paired request IDs for shadow traffic and tie to metrics pipeline
Run a cross-team pilot with two product teams and collect feedback
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after sync with Eng infra and Research. Initial scope agreed (Ava).
2025-02-21: Design mockups v0 shared in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/pm-99217-mockup (Design feedback from Priya: simplify cohort UI).
2025-02-24: Eng tech spike scheduled with ENG-21400 to validate sequential-test library choices (SPRT vs alpha-spending). Daniel to lead spike.
2025-02-27: Decided on alpha-spending approach for better control of Type I error across multiple looks; documented trade-offs in decision log.
2025-03-01: Security reviewed shadow-routing data flow; no PII leaves customer VPC for Private deployments. Marking security_review_required=false (Ava).
decision_log: 2025-02-24: Chose alpha-spending sequential testing over fixed-sample A/B due to unknown effect sizes and desire for early-stop in regressions.
2025-02-27: Default experiment template will include latency, top-k accuracy proxy, and error-rate. Customers can override with custom metrics.
2025-03-01: Auto-rollback actions limited to model routing rollback and alerting. No automatic code or infra rollback without human confirmation.
notes_for_engineering: Implement paired request IDs for shadow traffic to enable per-request comparison between control and candidate.
Traffic controller must expose a dry-run mode where routing decisions are logged but not applied (for safety).
Make rollback idempotent and observable: rollback events should include experiment id, model version, and timestamp.
Provide a simulation mode to estimate sample size and expected time-to-decision given historical traffic profiles.
